items.title: Papers: Amorim takes swipe at Man Utd players-turned-pundits
items.description: The top stories and transfer rumours from Saturday's newspapers...

items.title: Arsenal latest: Arteta striving to 'build the best club in the world'
Alonso: Benzema-like Joao Pedro is on same level as Haaland
items.description: Xabi Alonso has likened Joao Pedro to Karim Benzema and said the Chelsea striker is on the same level as Erling Haaland.

items.title: Tottenham latest: Richarlison fails to agree terms with Vasco da Gama
Richarlison could still leave Spurs - Saturday's gossip
items.description: Interest in Richarlison, Philippe Coutinho agrees Santos deal and Manchester United monitoring Adrien Truffert.

items.title: West Ham thrash Wrexham to go top of the Championship
items.description: West Ham made easy work of Wrexham in a 6-0 victory at the London Stadium to make it four in a row and go top of the Championship.

items.title: Bergvall signs new Spurs deal after uncertain future
items.description: Lucas Bergvall signs a new contract at Tottenham after telling the club he wanted to leave in the summer.

items.title: Like Benzema & as good as Haaland - Alonso on Joao Pedro
items.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso says striker Joao Pedro is similar stylistically to his former Real Madrid team-mate Karim Benzema and is at a comparable level to Manchester City's Erling Haaland.

items.title: Richarlison's move to Vasco da Gama falls through
items.description: Tottenham forward Richarlison's proposed move to Vasco da Gama falls through amid ongoing uncertainty over the Brazilian's future.

items.title: 'Beautifully worked, perfectly finished!' | Bowen strike opens the scoring
items.description: Jarrod Bowen opens the scoring for West Ham against Wrexham.

items.title: Kartal still Fenerbahce boss despite resigning
items.description: Ismail Kartal remains as head coach of Fenerbahce, despite resigning following Thursday's Champions League game with Roma.

items.title: Moroccan official told to stop making 2030 final promise
items.description: Morocco's prime minister tells the head of the country's football federation to stop making promises about the 2030 World Cup final, while the head of the Spanish federation says the showpiece should be played in Spain.
